newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar edges up in Tokyo, capped near 114.80 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar edges up in Tokyo, capped near 114.80 yen.

text.p: ASIAN FOREX ACTIVITY:
0002 GMT
*Dollar edges up against yen and mark in early Tokyo on buying from interbank operators and institutional investors, possibly life insurers, with short-covering emerging from around 114.35 yen.
*Some dealers said interbank buying also possible, but others said this still unlikely in any great amount.
*But topside expected to be capped near 114.80 yen on offers from exporters, lined up from that level on up to around 115 yen, dealers said.
*Upside bias developing in market after recent comments from Japanese and U.S. officials.

*Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of Japan Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, said on Tuesday that the pace of yen's rise against dollar was too rapid, while Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday that recent dollar moves were not a result of verbal intervention.

*U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Wednesday that U.S. administration's strong dollar policy would remain unchanged, and that strong dollar is "good" for economy as it leads to lower interest rates and lower inflation.
*Dealers said these comments helped create a climate that encouraged dollar buying.
*But when asked by reporters if dollar was currently strong, Rubin declined to comment, leaving some dealers wondering whether his statements were made merely to prevent a further dollar plunge.
*Most dealers said 114.80 yen likely to prove short-term resistance, with gains during Asian time expected to be limited to 115 yen at best.
*Any dips will provoke bargain-hunting bids, with such buying particularly likely just under 114 yen.

*Little impact expected from U.S. March trade data released on Wednesday, dealers said. Overall U.S. trade gap shrank to $8.5 billion in March, well below market forecasts for deficit in excess of $10.0 billion, but bilateral trade gap with Japan increased by 8.3 percent.

*In an interview with Reuters Financial Television broadcast Thursday, senior Bank of Japan (BOJ) official said that correction to yen's weakness has started, but pace has been too rapid. "Correction to the yen's excessive weakness has begun, but the pace has been too rapid," Takashi Anzai, executive director of the BOJ, said.
*"The market is in the process of finding the (yen) exchange levels that reflect fundamentals. We hope to see it (the yen's exchange rate) stabilise as soon as possible," he added.
*Anzai also said that uncertainties about Japan's financial system have now passed their peak, and that Japan's economy is now getting onto a recovery track.
*Participants in Tokyo mixed as to whether dollar has already hit bottom at 111.98 yen.
*One Japanese bank dealer said given steep fall of more than 16 yen from peak of 127.47 yen on May 1, three- to four-yen gains of dollar mere correction within downward trend.
*He said technical correction may push dollar as high as 119 yen, while others said dollar likely to be top-heavy around 116 yen due to possible sales by exporters.
*Japan's economic recovery not threatened as long as dollar remains between 110 and 120 yen, Makoto Utsumi, former vice finance minister for international affairs, said on Thursday.
0300 GMT
*Dollar edged up against yen by midday Tokyo on Thursday on steady short-covering and purchases by U.S. funds amid growing market perception that recent rapid drop in dollar has come to end for now.
*Dollar well-bid, helped by news that major Japanese bank made loss from derivatives trading at overseas branch, but topside remained heavy above 115 yen.
* News that Industrial Bank of Japan made 10 billion yen loss from derivatives trading sparked dollar purchases.
